content.title: Hundreds of High Point University students travel for NCAA tournament first round matchup
content.text: HIGH POINT, N.C. — More than 200 High Point University students loaded onto several buses and are traveling across the country to Portland, Oregon, to support the High Point Panthers men's basketball team from the sidelines of the Moda Center, in their first round matchup of the NCAA tournament against the No.5 seed Wisconsin Badgers.In the spirit of March Madness, the No.12 seed High Point University Panthers basketball team is going dancing for the second time in its program history after earning an automatic bid to the NCAA tournament after clinching its second consecutive Big South Championship title.HPU Basketball boasts a regular-season record of 30-4 (15-1 in conference play) and is catching fire at the right time; currently possessing a 14-game winning streak that dates back to Jan. 14 in a road matchup against Winthrop University.Since transitioning to a Division I program in 1999, High Point University has punched its ticket to the NCAA Tournament twice—both appearances coming back-to-back seasons (2024-25 and 2025-26).Entering this first-round matchup against the heavily-favored Wisconsin Badgers (-10.5 points according to ESPN), the High Point University Panthers have their sights on completing an upset and ruining the March Madness brackets of tens of millions across the nation.As these passionate students started to gather to board these buses, several were adamant that a 'Cinderella Run' to the next rounds of the tournament remains a possibility.Ryan Donaldson, a High Point University junior, is one of the hundreds of students who will be making the trip to support the Panthers in what many consider to be the biggest game in its program history. Donaldson recalls being in attendance for home games throughout the season, during which the Panthers posted a 17-1 home record, and stresses the importance of having this crowd support for a challenge such as the NCAA tournament.“It’s not home court advantage, but flying everybody out is going to feel pretty close to it," Donaldson said. "I’m just really grateful for the opportunity getting to cheer on our Panthers. You know, back-to-back years winning the Big South tournament. We were at the arena during the Selection Show [and] it's hard to put into words how awesome this all is."Donaldson also emphasizes that the university's approval of this travel opportunity reflects its unwavering commitment to ensuring students are part of this potentially historic moment.“It shows that they care, that High Point cares about us. You know, you’re not just a number here. I mean, we’re a smaller school, but we’re on the map now. I have a good feeling about it. We’re going to stay through Saturday, and watch them win on Saturday as well,” he said.Students are not the only ones making this trip across the country for this matchup.During the NCAA tournament selection show on Wednesday afternoon inside the Nido and Mariana Qubein Arena, High Point University surprised a local family of HPU superfans with an all-expenses-paid trip to watch the Panthers' first-round matchup against the Wisconsin Badgers.Alexis Ford, who will be attending this game with her three children and husband, describes this as a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity and anticipates an extended run throughout the tournament.“My husband picked on me by saying that I have too much stuff... it's because we’re going to be here for round two, baby!’" Ford said. "We’ve never flown before or been on a big trip like this. We’re a homeschooled family, so we get to go across [the country] for the biggest field trip of their lives."As this trip represents memories beyond the basketball court, Ford says this will be a full-circle moment for her family as they'll be able to root for their favorite team beyond the television.“I was telling him that it’s a whole moment, because we started coming here two seasons ago, and the first season we got attached, and we loved them. The second season, we got even more attached and loved them [too]," Ford said. "To go there every day, it was so exciting at their games, but to get to go to Portland to see them in like a big arena, we are just so proud to be a part of this moment."The tipoff for this first-round matchup of the NCAA tournament between the High Point Panthers and Wisconsin Badgers is scheduled for 1:50 p.m. EST inside the Moda Center.Back on campus, High Point University is hosting a watch party at 1 p.m. at the Slane Student Center to give other students who are staying behind a chance to gather and watch this matchup to potentially advance to the Round of 32.
